terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the report, and run callouts.py by itself to try its functions.

tasks.title: Move the reading functions
tasks.description:
Move `parts_of`, `hill_of` and `hours_of` from the top of `report.py` into `callouts.py`, so that they live in `callouts.py` only. Then, under `# Task 1` in `report.py`, import `hill_of` and `hours_of` from `callouts`, with `from` as the lesson shows (`import callouts` works too). Running `python3 report.py` prints the same four lines as before.

Check imports `callouts.py` the way an import line does, calls its `hill_of` and `hours_of` with lines of its own, looks at whether `report.py` still has functions of its own by those names, and runs `report.py` to see where its `hill_of` and `hours_of` come from.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson on a module of your own and on a circle of imports.
Cut the three functions from report.py and paste them into callouts.py, above crew_of.
Write the import line under # Task 1 in report.py.
Run python3 report.py and compare the four lines with what it printed before.
hints: A function takes with it everything it calls. Look at what `hill_of` and `hours_of` call before you choose what to move.

`callouts.py` must not import anything from `report.py`: `report.py` imports `callouts.py`, and an import back would go round in a circle. The import line names the module by its file name, without `.py`.
The shape is the three `def` blocks in `callouts.py`, and `from callouts import hill_of, hours_of` under `# Task 1` in `report.py`.

tasks.title: Nothing runs on import
tasks.description:
At the bottom of `callouts.py`, Ailsa's try-out lines print a line and what `crew_of` gives back for one line of the log. They run every time `report.py` imports `callouts`, in the middle of the report. Put them under a main guard, `if __name__ == "__main__":`, so that they run when `callouts.py` is run by itself and never when it is imported. Keep the lines as they are.

Check imports `callouts.py` and looks at what the import printed and which of your functions it called, then runs `python3 callouts.py` and looks for Ailsa's two lines.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on what runs when a file is imported.
Run python3 report.py and find Ailsa's lines in the middle of the report.
Write the guard above her try-out lines, and move both lines in under it.
Run python3 report.py, then python3 callouts.py, and compare what each prints.
hints: Importing a file runs every line of it at the top, not inside a def, once. A function's def only makes the function; a call or a print at the top runs.
Python sets `__name__` in every file: `"__main__"` in the file you ran, and the module's own name in a file that was imported. An `if` on it decides which lines run in which case.
The shape is `if __name__ == "__main__":` with Ailsa's two print lines moved in under it, four spaces each.

tasks.title: Hours on one hill
tasks.description:
In `callouts.py`, write a function called `hill_hours` that takes a list of lines of the callout log and a hill, and gives back the hours of every callout on that hill, added up, a whole number: `0` when there is none. Use `hill_of` and `hours_of`. Then, under `# Task 3` in `report.py`, import `hill_hours` from `callouts` and print what it gives back for `month` and `"Scarth Fell"`.

Check imports `callouts.py`, with its own `parts_of`, `hill_of` and `hours_of` set in it so that this task does not wait on Task 1, and calls `hill_hours` with lines and hills of its own, and looks at whether it called `hill_of` and `hours_of`.
nextSteps: Write the def line of hill_hours in callouts.py, above Ailsa's try-out lines.
Go through the lines, and add the hours of each line whose hill is the one asked for.
Import it in report.py and print the hours on Scarth Fell.
hints: Start a total at 0 before the loop, so a hill with no callouts gives back 0.
`hill_of(line)` gives the hill of one line, and `hours_of(line)` its hours as a number. They are in the same file, so `hill_hours` calls them by their names alone.
The shape is `total = 0`, then `for line in lines:` with `if hill_of(line) == hill:` and `total = total + hours_of(line)` under it, then `return total`.
